attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 1, pool timeouts 149

report.summary: A restart at 18:10:51 cut the DB pool from 10 connections/30 s timeout to 1/250 ms. A session idle in a transaction blocked the only connection, so borrowers timed out and transfers returned 5xx or ran slow.

findings.claim: The restart at 18:10:51 shrank the pool to a maximum of 1 connection with a 250 ms acquire timeout.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows poolMaximumSize 10→1 and poolConnectionTimeoutMs 30000→250 at the 18:10:51 restart.

findings.claim: The tiny pool caused connection acquisition timeouts, which match the transfer 5xx errors (22×500, 93×503, ~29% server errors) and the slow tail.
findings.reason: 149 acquisition timeouts at a 1-connection pool with 250 ms timeout; transfers show a 0.294 server-error ratio and p99 2.2 s.

findings.claim: A session idle in a transaction blocked another ledger_app session from 18:10:52 to 18:11:46, which worsens the pool starvation.
findings.reason: Session 89271 waited on session 89280 (idle in transaction) in 22 samples, with max wait ~2 s. With only 1 connection, any hold stalls all borrowers.

findings.claim: The outbox and consumer are not the cause: deliveries succeeded and were fast.
findings.reason: All 296 attempts succeeded (p95 88 ms). The outbox failed count stayed flat at 138, and the old undelivered age only grew with the clock.

limitations: A 10 s scrape gap at 18:10:43–18:10:53 straddles the restart, and counters reset, so the exact onset is blurred.
The source of the idle-in-transaction session 89280 is unidentified, and blocking is sampled only every 2 s.
